discovery: Discovery of Bose-Einstein condensation of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (mesoscopic and low-dimensional electron systems)
motivation: Eisenstein and co-workers showed experimentally that two closely spaced two-dimensional electron layers at total filling factor one form a coherent excitonic condensate. Their signatures were a giant Josephson-like peak in interlayer tunnelling, a quantized Hall drag, and vanishing counterflow resistance. MacDonald's theory predicted and explained this interlayer phase coherence as spontaneous symmetry breaking and exciton superfluidity. Pfeiffer's ultra-high-mobility GaAs/AlGaAs double quantum wells made these subtle many-body effects visible for the first time. This is a real macroscopic quantum state of excitons in a solid, found through careful heterostructure design and transport measurement. It started the continuing search for exciton condensates in electron-hole bilayers and in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide double layers. I nominate them together for combining clean materials, well-designed experiments and deep theory, which shows condensed matter physics at its best.
